text:
If you caught that clear sunset around 7:56, enjoy it, because the sky's about to flip. Clouds are already thickening ahead of a wet stretch that runs right through Monday. Showers move in between 8 and 10 tonight, then thunderstorms take over overnight, with a tenth to quarter inch of rain likely. If you're still out on the water, get in soon: a lake wind advisory is up, south winds building to 20 to 30 knots overnight with waves climbing to 2 to 4 feet, rough enough that broad-water boating should wrap up well before dark.

Monday's more of the same, showers likely before 1, then thunder chances picking up through the afternoon, mostly cloudy with a high near 77. The Euro is running much wetter than the American model on Monday, so I'd lean toward carrying the rain gear all day rather than betting on a dry window. Winds ease back to light and northerly by Monday night, and the good news is nothing looks severe. Air quality stays good, so it's just a matter of dodging the rain, not the smoke.
